description:
## Outcome

Trusted ceilings and data-safe run limits bound turns, time, usage, cost facts, cells, jobs, and provider concurrency. Exceeded limits produce portable evidence and stop new work safely.

## Why now

The current CLI uses infinite cell task timeout and a job count only. Constrained environments and validated records now make limit enforcement observable.

## Current state

Jidoka has `max_model_turns` and some runtime limits, but a capability can block. CLI `run.jobs` limits cell concurrency, while `Task.async_stream` uses infinite timeout. There is no maximum planned cells, per-provider admission, cell/suite deadline, or usage budget.

## Ownership and boundary

Both repositories change. Jidoka enforces per-turn and capability deadlines and reports observed usage. The CLI validates matrix and suite limits, applies stricter trusted host ceilings, controls cell/provider admission, and maps outcomes. Data can only reduce host ceilings.

## Detailed implementation

1. In Jidoka, define public applied-limit and limit-exceeded evidence for model turns, capability wall time, total sequence time, token/usage facts, and environment resource limits. Propagate cancellation to blocked capabilities.
2. In the CLI version-1 suite, add bounded `run.limits` for maximum planned cells, turns per cell, cell/suite duration, usage budget, and optional provider concurrency.
3. Resolve effective limits as the minimum of user request and trusted host ceiling. Reject attempts to raise a ceiling.
4. Preflight matrix size before opening artifacts. Admit cells by total jobs and provider key with deterministic fairness.
5. Stop new admission when suite deadline/budget is exhausted; cancel active work only under the documented policy.
6. Record requested, applied, observed, and stop reason in validated result/summary evidence.
7. Keep failure classification: unsafe configuration 64; limit reached during execution 1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oversized matrices and unsafe requested ceilings fail before execution.
- [ ] Blocked LLM, operation, extension, or environment call respects a capability deadline and cancellation.
- [ ] Provider concurrency never exceeds the applied limit.
- [ ] Cell/suite deadline and usage budget stop later work deterministically.
- [ ] Results distinguish requested, applied, observed, and exceeded facts.
- [ ] Existing runs without limits keep documented defaults.

## Test plan

- Success: bounded multi-provider matrix with injected counters and clocks.
- Invalid input: zero/negative/overflow limit, cells above ceiling, and user ceiling escalation.
- Runtime failure: blocked capability, limit timeout, budget exhaustion, cancellation failure, and provider queue error.
- Boundary and security: no later model/tool call after hard stop; environment confirmed limits must meet profile.
- Deterministic capability: virtual clock, admission probe, fake providers, usage counters, cancellation, and IDs.
- JSONL and exit status: applied/exceeded evidence, partial counts, stderr diagnostics, exit 1 for runtime limit and 64 for invalid configuration.

## Documentation

Update Jidoka runtime-limit and CLI suite guides. Add field tables, precedence, defaults, provider admission, partial run, and status rules.

## Non-goals

Do not implement price lookup, dynamic model routing, retries, or distributed rate limiting. Do not let data raise host limits.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.3.7` — Run each automation cell in one constrained environment
- `jido_cli-tqg.2.3` — Validate case results, manifests, and run summaries

Features unlocked by this story:

- Terminal partial-run integrity
- Safe large evaluation matrices

## Commit plan

Create exactly two focused commits because the repositories have separate histories. First create one `jidoka` commit such as `feat(jidoka): enforce bounded automation limits (jido_cli-tqg.6.3)`. Then create one `jido_cli` commit such as `feat(cli): integrate enforce bounded automation limits (jido_cli-tqg.6.3)`. Do not include another backlog feature in either commit.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/runtime/limits_test.exs test/jidoka/session_sequence_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jido_cli
mix test test/jido_cli/cli/automation/limits_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/automation_test.exs
mix quality
mix test --cover
mix docs
```
title: Enforce bounded runtime limits and provider-aware admission
